ev.q: Tennessee hospital discharge data documented a 27% decline in pneumonia hospitalizations
Rates were expressed as hospitalizations and ED visits per 1,000 children annually.
Annual pneumonia hospitalization rates in Tennessee children aged <2 years decreased from 14.5 to 4.1 per 1,000
Compared with PCV7 years, the rate after introduction of PCV13 was 27% lower
Annualized monthly rates were modeled using negative binomial regression accounting for seasonal variation.
this is an ecologic study that evaluated the impact of the U.S. PCV program in Tennessee
Pneumonia hospitalization rates were fairly stable in the pre-PCV period, declined substantially after PCV7 introduction

methods_quotes.q: Annualized monthly rates were modeled using negative binomial regression accounting for seasonal variation.
Relative rates (RR) were used to compare study periods and calculate percentage changes
Modelling rates over the three periods allowed estimation of linear trends in these three periods
Change in rates reflects changes in modeled trends and are not computed from rates displayed in columns 2–4.
